subject: Cloud Computing
title: Cloud Unit Economics
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Cloud Unit Economics.

hook.text: Your app costs $50,000/month in cloud. But what's the cost per user? Per transaction? That's unit economics.

buildup.text: Unit economics divides cloud cost by a business metric: cost per customer, per order, or per API call.

discovery.text: If each new customer costs $0.50/month in cloud, you can calculate exactly how revenue scales against cost.

twist.text: Total cloud cost can rise while unit cost drops. Growing efficiently means more customers for less per head.

climax.text: Unit economics turns cloud spending from a cost center conversation into a business growth conversation.

punchline.text: Total cost doesn't matter. Cost per customer does.

quiz.question: What do cloud unit economics measure?
options: Cloud cost relative to a business metric like cost per customer or transaction
The total monthly cloud bill divided by number of servers
How many data centers a cloud provider operates worldwide

details.summary: Cloud unit economics measures cost per business unit like cost per customer, per transaction, or per API call. This connects cloud spending to business value and reveals whether costs scale healthily as the business grows or are spiraling out of control.
details.whyItMatters: Absolute cloud spend always grows with a growing business. Unit economics reveals whether cloud efficiency is improving or degrading by normalizing cost against business metrics.
takeaways: Measures cost per customer, transaction, or business unit
Reveals whether cloud costs scale efficiently with growth
More meaningful than absolute spend for growing businesses

faq.question: What are good cloud unit economics metrics?
faq.answer: Cost per active user, cost per transaction, cost per thousand API calls, and infrastructure cost as a percentage of revenue. The best metric depends on your business model. SaaS companies often track cost per customer on a monthly basis.

faq.question: How do unit economics change as you scale?
faq.answer: Healthy scaling shows decreasing cost per unit as fixed costs are amortized and reserved pricing kicks in. If cost per unit increases, it often indicates architectural inefficiency, missing caching, or underutilized reservations that need attention.
